notes.title: 106 Fans' Ideas Turned into 8 Horror Stories
notes.content:
IN THE NEW FREE DLC, WE HAVE TURNED 106 FANS’ IDEAS INTO 8 HORROR STORIES!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44981917/115f8e56d4fecd0bd61059ccbcabd9976e567749.gif

Our goal was to include as many of your ideas in the game as possible. We read through over 600 suggestions, which took us many evenings. We did our best to understand how each idea would look in the game and whether it was possible to implement them based on how the game is built.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44981917/124cde8e909bd7239226067af2f00ae89622251b.gif{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44981917/7948e3035be97bf21f8e3bae7a7a4b4b8d450073.gif{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44981917/93559f1561938e7f724d7761adadf3347aa642d2.gif{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44981917/1ddde79b68e93ca86c6e9d7a20e67cdaa2fcfe1c.gif{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44981917/2bb1a2ffddf61c0a653bf870a2536470d2e393a4.gif{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44981917/43b327d0e6756f2afefb9e6039bf36320b0f7ad5.gif

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44981917/de4cf6a138ba21c16238403c864f6335d4fef05e.jpg
Curious to know whose idea made it into the game? Here's a screenshot of the DLC’s credits. (At the top, we're animated, applauding everyone whose idea was included.)

We've made a short video where we talk about the process of creating this free DLC:

[previewyoutube=mii1niBzlPo;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]











WE SELECTED IDEAS BASED ON THE FOLLOWING CRITERIA:

1.	Ideas we thought were scary, funny, beautiful, or unique.
2.	We didn’t select ideas that were too similar to something we already had in the game.
3.	We wanted to combine ideas from different people.

(If we didn’t use your idea, it doesn’t mean it was a bad idea—it likely just didn’t fit within these three criteria.)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44981917/e1f5c07514a2a69c40644b6dc069374387a631a9.gif

It's been a lot of fun—and a lot of hard work—creating these 8 horror stories based on your ideas! We will now focus on our next game, Unsound Love, which you can wishlist here:
Unsound Love

If you'd like us to create more stories for Security: The Horrible Nights, let us know by writing a Steam review, sharing the game with others, and giving this post a thumbs up! We need a break from the game right now, but if we feel there's a big interest for more stories, we might consider making a very special extra DLC!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44981917/b1361f1d0f75cfe9138f7f181db90ef2b973208e.gif

Thanks to EVERYONE who shared an idea!
— John & Maria

notes.title: We won the award for BEST NARRATIVE!
notes.content:
We won the award for BEST NARRATIVE at Spilprisen 2025 (the Danish game award show)!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44981917/1fd6b43679c0a822e21f165d99350917af8178d1.jpg

We were also nominated for: Best Game Design, Best Audio, Best Visuals and Game of The Year. We were very pleased to win an award, and were especially happy that it was BEST NARRATIVE, because it's not just about the written story, but how it's conveyed. Everyone on the team has therefore been an important part of this, as we consist of John (writer and designer), Maria (art and animation) and Astrid (music composer).

AND YES! IT WAS SUPER WEIRD TO HAVE TO GO UP AND RECEIVE AN AWARD IN A BIG HALL FULL OF PEOPLE! We would have become actors and not game developers if we felt comfortable on a stage with a lot of lights. ;)

At the show itself, we met people from Playdead (Limbo, Inside), Geometric Interactive (Cocoon), Triband (WHAT THE GOLF?) and Ghost Ship Games (Deep Rock Galactic). They were all super nice and shared some stories from their own productions.

If you've played our game, Anglerfish, these are some of the Danish gaming companies that we parodied at the start of the game. So, it was cool to talk to them for real, and to hear from one of them that they had played Anglerfish and liked it. We didn't really expect any of them to ever play Anglerfish, so this person immediately became our new best friend!

However, it was almost cooler to talk to some of the other small indie developers in our home country. For example, we met Quack People, who were nominated for Best Debut for their ‘The Duck Pond’, which is a cute little idle/clicker game you should probably click on if you're into that kind of games. :)

We also spoke to the small indie team Guidelight Games, who won Game of the Year with SpellRogue. Although they snapped the award right under our noses, we thought they seemed like super nice guys and we have a lot of respect for all the hard work they put into making SpellRogue. If you're into deckbuilding/dice games and haven't already checked out their game, hurry up and do it!

Now we're back in the office, where we've just had the first day of production on our new game. It's called ‘Unsound Love’ and you can wishlist it on Steam already, even though it hasn't been officially announced. So right now, award shows feel far away when you're right back at the start of a new process. We will also soon be test playing the free DLC 2 for Security: The Horrible Nights, as we have done all the stories for that DLC now. :o

However, there's a lot of polishing to do before that DLC is ready for you to play, so you'll hopefully have a good experience.

Thanks again to everyone who bought, supported, reviewed and shared their favorite story from Security: The Horrible Nights!
- John & Maria

notes.title: FREE DLC - Stories by horror experts OUT NOW!
notes.content:
The first free DLC is out now! Once you have added it to your account, you will find the new stories under ‘more stories’.

[previewyoutube=c8g6YUEM5rs;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










Security: The Horrible Nights is a horror anthology, so we had a dream of bringing in guest storytellers, as the variety of voices is one of the things we love about this format. We had a wishlist of 5 voices we wanted to include, and 4 of them are in this DLC! The final voice is the players, which will be the second free DLC. It is still possible to make suggestions for this DLC. Remember to keep it short and not too much detail, as this will increase your chances of being included. We're looking for ideas that surprise us either in a scary or funny way!
Make a story for the game

Can you survive the stories from our horror experts?

ManlyBadassHero, who has played more indie horror games on his YouTube channel than most. He almost always ends his videos with a short reflection on what makes the game good and bad. He has played several of our previous games. We were super excited to see what he could come up with, with his vast experience, and we are pretty happy with what his story ended up being.

The Mason Scale is our personal favorite horror game reviewer. If you're into horror games, check out his YouTube channel, where there are plenty of reviews. You can clearly feel his love for psychological horror in his story. It's been a lot of fun trying to bring his eerie ideas to life.

Alpha Beta Gamer was the first to share our very first horror game, the 6-minute long The ER. Ever since, we've returned again and again to his website and YouTube channel, because here you'll find just loads of indie horror gold. He also came up with a classic, crazy and super 80s horror story, which was super cool because that's the period the game is inspired by.

Mathias Clasen is a horror researcher at Aarhus University. He is the author of “Why Horror Seduces” and “A Very Nervous Person's Guide to Horror Movies”. He will be on the radio in the game where he will answer questions like: Is a horror film a good date film? What are the positive effects of playing horror games? And many other thrilling things he has learned through his research. Maria, our graphic designer, used our first horror game (The ER) as part of her bachelor project at university. She used a text by Mathias Clasen in her project, so he has inspired us since the beginning, so it was great to have him in the game.

We hope you enjoy the DLC, and let us know which story you liked best. We're curious.
- John & Maria
Professional Villains

notes.title: Security: The Horrible Nights - First week!
notes.content:
Security: The Horrible Nights has now been out for a week, and a lot has happened!
It's been a crazy week! We want to share what has happened, what’s going to happen, and say thank you.

We're thrilled to hear that many of you have enjoyed the game! That’s why we make games. :)
Thanks to everyone who reviewed the game, and a special thank you to those who mentioned in your reviews which story you liked best—because we’re curious. Thanks also to everyone who has shared the game with others. It’s tough to get noticed as a small indie developer, so we deeply appreciate your support. <3

The game is now version 1.10

We believe we’ve fixed the bugs you’ve reported. Thank you for your feedback! (And we’re ready to fix more if you encounter any!)

We’ve been watching, listening, and reading about your experiences with the game, and based on that, we’ve made several small adjustments and additions to improve the experience. Some examples include:

•	You can now also hold down SHIFT to run.
•	Instead of needing to hold the run button for 5 seconds to run extra fast, you now only need to hold it for 3 seconds.
•	We’ve clarified certain things/events that some players missed.
•	SPOILER: [spoiler]We’ve made your patients behind the red door move 20% faster.[/spoiler]

Other interesting things that have happened

•	Over 4000 stories have been survived!
•	Boshea has created The Security Survival Guide, so help is now always within reach! (Find it under Guides here on Steam.)
•	We still haven’t seen anyone steal a drink from the boss’s minibar in his office. (You’re obviously very well-behaved.)
	
What happens next?
We’ll, of course, continue fixing bugs reported in the bug thread here on Steam.

The soundtrack for the game will be released in a week!

We’re also working on the first free DLC, featuring stories by horror experts. We’ll be interviewing Mathias Clasen, a horror researcher at Aarhus University and author of A Very Nervous Person's Guide to Horror Movies, which explores research on how horror affects us. Interestingly, there are many positive effects of experiencing horror. Be sure to wishlist the DLC to get notified when it releases early next year.

The second free DLC will feature stories based on fan ideas. If you have a horror story idea you’d like to see in the game, there’s a link here to submit it for consideration.
https://steamcommunity.com/app/2911390/discussions/0/4514379280323767599/


Otherwise, enjoy your work as a security guard!
- John & Maria
Professional Villains

notes.title: 70 fans' ideas turned into 4 stories!
notes.content:
We've read through over 500 horror ideas from you through our Discord, the game's Steam page, and Manly Badass Hero's video playing the demo.

We selected over 70 ideas and turned them into 4 unique horror stories. You can try them out now in the free prologue called Security: Stories by the fans:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3199440/Security_Stories_by_the_fans/?l=danish&curator_clanid=40000720

If you play the 4 stories, be sure to write a Steam review mentioning which one of the 4 is your favorite. Because we're super curious to hear which one people like the best! :D

We will make more stories based on fan ideas. There are several here on the game's Steam page that we already really like and would love to do that we couldn’t fit in the prologue. So, it's still possible for you to get your idea into the game! You have the best chance of getting your idea included if you answer the questions in this thread:
https://steamcommunity.com/app/2911390/discussions/0/4514379280323767599/

Short, precise ideas are more likely to be included than long, detailed descriptions.

We will make a free DLC with more stories based on fan ideas after we release Security: The Horrible Nights in November. The more wishlists we have, the more additional stories we can make. So, remember to wishlist the game and maybe get a friend to do the same. ;)

It's been both fun and challenging to create the four stories based on fan ideas. We can't wait to read what else you come up with!
- John & Maria
Professional Villains

We will be making a free standalone DLC that will be released sometime after the game is released, where all the stories are based on fans' ideas. Or a small story idea that you'd like to see John, our designer, writer and programmer, bring to life?

We've created a thread where we ask 5 questions for you to answer that will help you to tell us your idea in a way that increases the chance that we can get it in the game. It is also in this thread you have to write your ideas. Link to the thread here:
Make a story for the game!

It's definitely an advantage to play the demo first to get an idea of the game. And remember to WISHLIST the GAME because: ‘The more wistlists = more extra stories we can make’

We can't wait to hear what you think of the demo and read what ideas you have for a horror story in the game!
- John & Maria

notes.title: DEMO coming soon!
notes.content:
We've been working on a spooky demo that will give you a good idea of what to expect from the final game. We've even thrown in a little teaser of some of the game's secrets that some of you might discover.

Some fast facts about the demo:

•	At the end of the demo, there is a big reveal!
•	The demo will be available in all 17 languages.
•	You can play with keyboard and mouse or with a controller.
•	We've filled the demo with surprises, so it should be a good time for both gamers and let's players.

We're really excited for you to try our game because, based on the playtesters' reactions, the demo should both scare you a bit and make you laugh. We're also thrilled for you to hear all the music Astrid Fabrin has created for your in-game radio and to experience Maria's many animated death scenes.
We're currently fine-tuning and extra testing the demo to ensure it runs well for you!

We hope you're ready to try not to die in our demo soon. But should you die, remember:
“Every time you die, a new story begins.”
- John & Maria
